United States.text: In 1951 a reactor in the Idaho desert lit four light bulbs: the first usable electricity from nuclear fission.
United States.evidence: In the early afternoon of December 20, 1951, Argonne director Walter Zinn and fifteen other Argonne staff members witnessed a row of four light bulbs light up in a nondescript brick building in the eastern Idaho desert. ... This was the first time that a usable amount of electrical power had ever been generated from nuclear fission.

China.text: Over 38 more reactors are being built here, the most of any country for the 18th year running.
China.evidence: At the same time, there are over 38 reactors under construction with a total net capacity of 38 GWe, ranked first for the 18th consecutive year.

France.text: Nuclear power made 71.67% of its electricity in 2018, the highest share in the world.
France.evidence: Since the mid-1980s, the largest source of electricity in France has been nuclear power ... In 2018, the nuclear share was 71.67%, the highest percentage in the world.

Russia.text: The world's first nuclear power plant, a 5 MW one at Obninsk, joined the Soviet grid in 1954.
Russia.evidence: the world’s first nuclear power plant, with a capacity of 5 MW at Obninsk in the Soviet Union was connected to the public supply in 1954

South Korea.text: Its first nuclear plant, Kori, opened in 1978; nuclear now makes 31% of its electricity.
South Korea.evidence: Kori Nuclear Power Plant was the first plant in Korea to commence commercial operations in 1978. ... In 2025, nuclear power produced 31% of the country’s electricity.

India.text: Asia's first nuclear reactor, Apsara, started up here in August 1956.
India.evidence: India's and Asia's first nuclear reactor, Apsara, reached criticality at 3:45 p.m. on 4 August 1956 and was inaugurated by Prime Minister Nehru on 20 January 1957.

Canada.text: Its reactors burn natural uranium; in 1945 its ZEEP pile made the first chain reaction outside the US.
Canada.evidence: on September 5, 1945, at 3:45 p.m., the 10-watt ZEEP achieved the first self-sustained nuclear reaction outside the United States. ... Canada is a technology leader in heavy water reactors and natural uranium fueled reactors more broadly.

Japan.text: Besides its 15 in use, 18 of its reactors are suspended: most of the 23 suspended in the whole world.
Japan.evidence: The table (Country | Reactors / In use | Reactors / Suspended): World | 428 | 23 ... Japan | 15 | 18. The other suspended reactors are India's 4 and Pakistan's 1.

Ukraine.text: Its 15 include Zaporizhzhia's six, Europe's largest plant, seized by Russian forces in March 2022 and now shut.
Ukraine.evidence: There are four nuclear power plants in Ukraine but one of them, Zaporizhzhia, is now occupied and claimed by Russia and shutdown. The 15 reactors total installed capacity is over 13 GWe. ... one of the six reactors of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant ... Zaporizhzhia is the largest nuclear power plant in Europe ... In March 2022, Russian forces seized control of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant.

United Kingdom.text: Calder Hall, opened in 1956, was the first nuclear plant to make electricity in commercial amounts.
United Kingdom.evidence: Calder Hall was the world's first nuclear power station to deliver electricity in commercial quantities (although the world’s first nuclear power plant, with a capacity of 5 MW at Obninsk in the Soviet Union was connected to the public supply in 1954).
